slides.title: AlphaEarth Foundations
slides.text:
- A model designed to function as a virtual satellite whose images summarize Earth’s surface dynamics over space and time
- Learn meaningful patterns across data streams and generate spatially and temporally precise embedding vectors for any place, any time
- Outputs designed for practitioners – like an AI-powered image composite
- Embedding images are a foundation on which many different EO applications can be built

📑 Read more in our preprint here: arxiv.org/abs/2507.22291

slides.title: Summary: Similarity Search
slides.text:
- Compare embedding vector for a sampled location and every other location @ 10-meter resolution
- Generate a map of similarity scores on-demand
- Sample multiple points to define semantics
- Resample (average) embeddings to aggregate to patch scales (using any rules you like!)

slides.title: Similarity in time = stability
slides.text:
- Compare embedding vector for a sampled location with vector for that location for a different year
- Use similarity as a measure of relative stability/instability
- Consistency objective incentivizes overall stability, however individual axes may (jointly) encode responses in different properties
- Change can mean “surface change” or it could be “environmental change”, i.e., wet year versus dry year

slides.title: Settlement 2025
slides.notes:
You can also use dot product similarity to compare embedding vectors for the same location for different years

Here, we can think of “similarity” as a measure of relative stability (or instability)

And remember – AlphaEarth Foundations includes a consistency objective that incentivizes stability through time (regardless of inputs / spacing / sensor availability), which means embeddings are comparable from year-to-year

However, as we noted for spatial similarity search, embeddings encode a complex combination of spatial, temporal and measurement properties, so it’s best to think of change in terms of both environmental and surface conditions

slides.title: Classification & regression
slides.text:
Embedding vector

- Linear separability great for clustering and tree-based classification/regression
- Substitute embeddings for other spatiotemporal features (e.g., composites, harmonics) in existing workflows
- No preprocessing required!
- Easily scale results using EE

Classifier

Classification

slides.title: Summary:
slides.text:
n=948 samples

n=948 samples

- Expect better performance with fewer observations, excellent performance with large, high-quality datasets
- Legends that previously may not have been possible
- Better handling of rare classes
- Scale field measurements from intensely measured sites
- Wall-to-wall annotations and large chip-based datasets not required
- Can also handle continuous variables / regression approaches

slides.title: Wrap-up: Good practices
slides.text:
- Prioritize quality over quantity
- Match labels to years
- “Annualize” labels
- Points easier to work with than polygons for mapping
- Use mean embeddings to classify polygons or patches
- Keep in mind you’re working in unit-length (learned) vector space
